summary.headline: Borosil Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR253.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 14.6% from 17.8% on a ~INR10 crore West Asia cost hit.
summary.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations grew 9% YoY to INR253.6 crore, with Glassware up 16.8% and Non-glassware up 4.2%, both stated as volume-led. Operating EBITDA fell to INR35.9 crore from INR40.2 crore as fuel and packaging inflation from the West Asia conflict hit margins; management said price increases of 5-7% were taken but realisations lag into Q2 onwards. PBT dropped to INR17.4 crore from INR23.5 crore (last year included a INR7.2 crore one-time stamp duty reversal), and PAT fell to INR12.8 crore from INR17.4 crore. Management reiterated an FY27 EBITDA margin of about 18% excluding other income, and a steady-state ambition of 18% without the conflict impact.</overview>

segments.name: Larah Opalware
segments.commentary: Sales INR83.6 crore, up 9.8% YoY from INR76.2 crore, stated as volume-led with hardly any price contribution. Management guides roughly 9% growth going forward.

segments.name: Glassware (borosilicate microwavables, serveware, tumblers, lunch boxes, storage)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR65.6 crore, up 16.8% YoY from INR56.2 crore; management said growth was entirely volume-led with price pass-through lagging. Utilisation about 90%.

segments.name: Non-glassware (small appliances, bottles and flasks, cookware, kitchen essentials)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR98.1 crore, up 4.2% from INR94.2 crore. Hydra (vacuum flasks) remained hit by BIS compliance requirements, offset by domestic appliances and stainless steel cookware.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 18%, excluding other income; management framed 14-15% historically and ~18% as the steady-state level without West Asia impact.
FY27 capex estimated at about INR125 crore, with an overall range of INR125-150 crore including solar and opal furnace rebuild maintenance capex.
FY27 consolidated depreciation expected at about INR92 crore.
Solar Phase 3 savings estimated at INR27-28 crore at EBITDA level in FY27; management declined to say how much would be retained after pass-through.
Price realisation from the 5-7% increases expected to flow in from Q2 FY27 onwards.
Long-term ROCE aspiration of 20-24% (later referenced as 20-22%) on the business; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Stylenest India (subsidiary) Hydra plant in Rajasthan: 2 double-wall lines commenced commercial production on 30 June 2026; third line expected in Q2 FY27.

Third captive solar plant in Bikaner: 20 MWp with battery energy storage, commissioned in Q1 FY27; solar now meets about 61% of energy requirement. Further 6.5 MWp (Borosil) and 3-4 MWp (Stylenest) solar under evaluation.
Bharuch, Gujarat glassware plant: capex INR42 crore, sanctioned in Q4 FY26 to make jugs, jars and bottles currently sourced (~INR100 crore sales) from BSL Bharuch; commissioning by end Q3 FY27.

Jaipur borosilicate pressware blast furnace expansion from 25 to 32 tons per day plus a third forming line; capex INR50 crore; commissioning by end Q4 FY28. Current furnace utilisation about 90%; furnace rebuild due Jan 2028.
Opalware utilisation described as full; Glassware about 90%.
demand_pricing: Price increases of 5-7% by category taken across multiple categories (management says some above that); execution started mid-May and realisation lags into Q2.
West Asia conflict net impact on Q1 FY27 about INR10 crore (INR12 crore cited in Q&A), with price increases compensating only a couple of crore.

Fuel cost run-rate: Opalware fuel impact about INR6 crore in Q1, expected to fall to about INR1.5 crore a quarter; borosilicate fuel impact about INR2.5 crore a quarter, expected to fall to INR60-70 lakh. Fuel at 5.8% of sales vs 2.9% a year ago.
Chinese dumping in borosilicate glassware persists despite rupee depreciation and higher freight; anti-dumping investigation pending with authorities, timing uncertain and not included in guidance.
Whiteware (Opalware sub-category) about 10% of Opalware sales vs under 5% last year; management said margins are well below the regular range, so it will not push that mix up.

Omnichannel presence across 24,000+ retail outlets, e-commerce, quick commerce and B2B/export; first two exclusive Borosil brand stores opened in Pune and Gurugram, Jaipur next, capex INR40-50 lakh per store, no store-count target.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Glassware's 16.7% growth was price vs volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was entirely volume-led; price pass-through is lagging and was only a couple of crore in Q1 against about INR12 crore West Asia impact. Price hikes range 5-7% by category.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 margin and capex guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% EBITDA margin for FY27 excluding other income; capex about INR125 crore, with a range up to INR150 crore including solar and furnace maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Has Chinese dumping eased given rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management says dumping continues with no visible difference despite rupee weakness and higher freight. Anti-dumping investigation is ongoing, and no benefit is assumed in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 growth inflated by channel inventory stocking ahead of price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management rejected that view, saying price impact arrives only in Q2 and there was no forced sale or retailer stocking. Inventory build is typical ahead of Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in ~18% margin given historical 14-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that 14-15% is the historical level and ~18% is the steady-state margin without West Asia impact; FY27 target is for 18% on the year, with improvement dependent on price realisation and lower fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to 20-24% ROCE and why is ROCE around 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed low ROCE to heavy capex over three to four years, plus inventory built for BIS challenges. It described 20-24% as a medium-term aspiration; it did not provide a bridge or timeline.
